slides.headline: China launched its first foreign astronaut
slides.subline: **A Pakistani pilot** is on his way to China’s Tiangong space station.
slides.credit: ForrestXYC, photoshopped by Ib / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Shenzhou-13 launch, file photo)

slides.body: Shenzhou-24 lifted off on a **Long March-2F** rocket from the Jiuquan centre in the Gobi Desert at 8:18 am local time. China called it a [[complete success]].
Pakistani pilot [[Muhammad Zeeshan Ali]] is the **first foreigner** to fly on a Chinese crewed mission. “I carry the **hopes of 250 million** Pakistanis,” he said.
His trip is a **brief visit**. He will return to Earth with Shenzhou-23 crew members **Lai Ka-ying**, Hong Kong’s first astronaut, and Zhang Zhiyuan.
Shenzhou-23 commander **Zhu Yangzhu** stays on board for [[a full year]]. Reuters says it will be the longest single stay by a Chinese astronaut.
China aims to land astronauts on the Moon by **2030**; the US is aiming for 2028. Should space stations be open to every country? Tell us below.
